results.summary_before: This Verilog design controls a 16x2 HD44780-compatible LCD in 4-bit data mode and displays a hardcoded funny message. It requires a 50 MHz clock and an active-low reset, and its pins are named to match the LCD signals for direct wiring. After reset is released the message should appear on the screen. The only external hardware needed is the 16x2 LCD module itself.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design implements an 8-bit linear feedback shift register that produces a new pseudo-random value on each read. A seed can be loaded by placing a value on the input pins and pulsing the write-enable pin, or the register can be reset with the chip reset. Testing consists of reading the output pins repeatedly and confirming that each value differs from the last. The design is a simple, self-contained PRNG block requiring no external hardware.

It is intended for testing and debugging of digital circuits.

results.summary_before: This project implements an adaptive leaky integrate-and-fire spiking neuron core for edge AI. It features a 12-bit membrane potential with configurable decay, adaptive threshold, and a 3-cycle refractory period. The design outputs the membrane potential, spike, and spike count. It is intended for low-power neural network applications and includes learning mode control.

results.summary_before: This is a 4-bit carry look-ahead adder implemented in Verilog. It takes two 4-bit operands and a carry input, and produces a 4-bit sum and a carry output. The design is purely combinational and can be used as a building block for larger adders. It was tested on an FPGA, and no external hardware is required.
